Свои домены выводятся двумя путями сразу:
Custom domains are routed outside in two ways at once. The first is route exclusion: upon connection, the name is resolved to addresses, and they are excluded from the tunnel. Requires Android 13 and newer, and the exclusion is computed once at connection time — edits to the list during an active session will take effect only after reconnecting. The second is using the same engine as zones: the name is matched against intercepted DNS responses. It works on any Android version, but only on WARP and MASQUE, only for TCP on ports 80 and 443, and only with encrypted DNS enabled. The rule applies to the full name and its subdomains — ozon.ru covers market.ozon.ru, but not 67ozon.ru.

Zones: addresses are learned from intercepted DNS responses, and matching connections go outside bypassing the tunnel. Works only on WARP and MASQUE (on Opera and VLESS, traffic is handled by tun2proxy, and the core does not see it) and only for TCP on ports 80 and 443. QUIC (HTTP/3) goes through the tunnel and reaches its destination — meaning bypass does not apply to it at all, and there will be no fallback to TCP. At most 256 addresses are remembered at a time; the oldest are evicted. Requires encrypted DNS enabled: without interception, zone addresses cannot be discovered.

Worth knowing: a bypassed zone means trusting the entire zone. The owner of any name in it can point it to any address, and that address will bypass the VPN. Addresses are taken only from responses to queries for names in your rules; unrelated records in the same response are discarded — but the “bypass the entire zone” rule itself is broader than a list of domains. Also, bypass works by address: if other names reside on a learned address (shared CDN, anycast), their traffic will also bypass the tunnel.

What bypasses the VPN

Honestly and without fine print: the proxy only forwards TCP connections. Your system sends everything else directly, using its regular address.

  • Online games, voice and video calls. Almost always UDP — the proxy does not forward such traffic.
  • QUIC and HTTP/3. Also UDP. When a proxy is configured, browsers usually fall back to standard TCP automatically, but not all and not always.
  • System DNS queries. Domain names opened via the proxy are resolved by the phone itself — using DNS rules configured in Nova. However, queries from apps that do not use the proxy go to your standard DNS, and the provider will see which domains you access. The app cannot bind to the standard DNS port on the phone: that is a system port requiring root privileges.
    Tip: if your client settings allow choosing between SOCKS5 and SOCKS5h — choose socks5h. Then the domain name is sent to the phone entirely and resolved by it. Standard socks5 resolves the domain locally first and only then routes via proxy.
  • Apps without proxy support. System proxy settings are not mandatory for all apps: torrent clients, some games, and utilities ignore them.
  • Local network. Router, printer, and network drives remain accessible directly — as intended.

If you need absolutely everything, including UDP, to go through the VPN, the device itself must run a VPN client. Sharing without root cannot do this in any app — this is a limitation of Android, not Nova.

Что это. Первый пакет встроенного профил:
What this is. The first packet of a built-in profile pretends to be the start of a QUIC connection to another domain — this domain is what the provider sees instead of WireGuard. In firmware it is the same for all profiles, but networks differ: in some places DPI already flags it, in others it does not pass at all.

What adaptation does. It picks another domain for the profile from the “SNI masking” list: one profile every half hour and no earlier than five minutes after the screen turns off. The network is not touched at all during this — regular connection will verify the selected domain, and if traffic does not flow, the hostname is removed.
